query: The Cold Range {No steam on Mabel's windows, and no smell of toast. The range behind the counter has gone out, and a queue of students in scarves is stamping its feet. "No tea till it's lit, petal," says Mabel, rattling the grate.|The range is out again: the flue sulks in a north wind. Mabel looks at the queue, then at you, then at the coal bucket.|Mabel's range, cold again, and Mabel in front of it with a twist of paper. "It knows you now," she says. "Talk to it."} Fetch coal from the yard {You haul two buckets in from the frozen yard. When the kettle finally sings, Mabel pours yours first and waves your coins away.|Two buckets, one dropped on your foot. The range catches on the third try, and Mabel puts a scone by your cup, "for the foot".|You fetch the coal without being asked. Mabel tells the queue you're "staff, near enough", and makes you carry the milk.} Read in the cold till it's lit {You read a chapter in your coat while the queue grumbles. By the time the tea comes your fingers can't turn the page.|You read by the cold window. The chapter is good; the draught under the door is better at its job.|Coat on, book open, breath fogging. You learn a great deal and feel your toes rather less.} Light it with a finger {You lean over the counter and touch the coals. The range roars, the queue cheers, and Mabel calls you "a useful sort of petal" for the rest of the term.|A flick, and the flue draws like a chimney in a storybook. Mabel pours your cup first and doesn't charge, "for services to tea".|{spell_level(flame) >= 2: You light the range and the lamps and the kettle's underside, one, two, three. Mabel applauds with the tea towel.|You light it before Mabel has finished asking. She gives you a look that's half thanks, half "show-off".}}
